answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can verify identities via acoustic time-of-flight localization. As nodes wander across a coastal lagoon, transceivers measure acoustic reflections off a seabed canyon to triangulate unique physical coordinates. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of provisioning discrete acoustic payloads and hulls per identity. However, thermocline shifts and salinity gradients distort sound velocity, occasionally rejecting honest nodes.
